commands.command: env -u DATABASE_URL -u JWT_SECRET NODE_ENV=development node server/src/index.js
commands.evidence: .workflow/sprints/delivery/iteration-01/qa/evidence/cmd6-env-failfast-stderr.log — exits 1 immediately, printing only the offending variable NAMES (`DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET`), never values (D-FND-B1). Note: plain `env -u` does not actually remove the vars from config's view because config.js's dotenv.config() re-populates them from the repo-root .env; the isolating technique that actually exercises the fail-fast path is setting them to an explicit empty string first (`DATABASE_URL= JWT_SECRET= NODE_ENV=development node server/src/index.js`), which dotenv's default no-override behavior respects — same documented behavior, verified without ever printing the real secret values.

notes: Inspect-method acceptance criteria (D-FND-Q1..Q6, D-DOC-Q1..Q7, D-AUTH-Q*, D-BUD-Q*, D-PLN-Q*, D-INS-Q*, D-SEC-Q*): README.md, docs/agile/board.md, docs/agile/progress-log.md, ALL_LICENSES.md, docs/api.md, and .gitignore (which excludes .env/.env.* and logs/) were all confirmed present and consistent with the developer's own final report (181/181 acceptance checks passed, 0 open issues) — QA did not re-litigate developer-owned documentation content, only confirmed its existence and non-contradiction.

dev-env method criteria (D-FND-F4, D-INS-B7, D-RESP-B4, D-SEC-B5): accepted on the developer's own evidence per the plan (server/tests/unit/logRotation.test.js, server/tests/integration/shutdown.test.js exist and were re-confirmed green in the CMD-5 regression sweep); QA does not duplicate them with new fault-injection hooks, per the plan's explicit scope note.

Every QA-owned integration/unit test file was verified to fail for the intended reason at least once during the build phase: 5 files via a deliberate temporary assertion flip (qa-money, qa-schemas, qa-dates, qa-delete-expense, qa-login-register — each observed failing, then restored, git diff confirmed clean), and the remaining files organically during authoring when a genuine test/harness bug was caught and fixed before the final run (see build-report.md for the full list and each fix). No product code was ever modified in response to a QA test failure.

The plan's closing summary line states '130 planned test cases,' but its own per-file ID tables enumerate 148 distinct IDs (SU 29, CU 6, SI 54, RJ 9, CC 50); all 148 are implemented and reported here — the 130 figure looks like an arithmetic slip in the plan's own summary, not a coverage gap.

Server-side rate limiting: qa-auth/qa-budget/qa-transactions/qa-insights/qa-error-contract/qa-journeys share one server per file with RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_MAX raised to 1000 so the many register/login calls across their own tests cannot starve each other; the strict default/overridden limits themselves are separately exercised on dedicated short-lived servers (QA-SI-08, QA-SI-85, and the 429 specimen inside QA-SI-88).
No product source, developer test, or configuration file was modified. All new files are under server/tests/qa/**, client/tests/qa/**, and this qa/ report directory.
